protections: Inbound webhook dispatch is authenticated by comparing the caller-supplied Authorization 'Bearer <token>' value against the secret TONAPI issued for the endpoint that the request path resolves to, inside TonapiWebhookDispatcher.process() (pytonapi/webhook/dispatcher.py:286-288); the only producer of those secrets is setup() (pytonapi/webhook/dispatcher.py:106-112).

A request path with no registered handler is rejected before parsing or dispatch (pytonapi/webhook/dispatcher.py:282-284); this routing guard is what the auth check is keyed on, and it is fed by the same path map.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: setup() only ever creates one webhook per event type at the default suffix (dispatcher.py:109-111) and stores the token under that suffix path (112), so TONAPI never issued a secret for a custom path; a missing _tokens entry therefore reads as 'there is nothing to verify' and the check at 286-287 is skipped.

A handler registered after setup() is outside the documented register-then-setup order; the token producer (setup, 106-112) is not re-run when registration resets the path map (260, 343), and no TONAPI webhook exists for the new path yet, so there is nothing to verify.

teardown(cleanup=True) is best-effort unsubscribe and subscriptions are documented to persist across restarts (docs/webhooks/guide.mdx:166), so a webhook that cleanup fails to match is a lifecycle wart rather than a security failure.

Only handlers[0][2] is kept per event type (dispatcher.py:170, 182), so any further path is rejected as 'Unknown webhook path' at 283-284 — a fail-closed outcome for an undocumented shape (several distinct paths for one event type), so the truncation looks harmless.

If the application builds its own webhooks through the low-level client (client.py:115-125) and never calls setup(), the dispatcher was never handed any token; verifying there is the application's job, and tokenless dispatch with no client is the documented and tested mode (tests/webhook/test_dispatcher.py:60-83, 131-141).

Two event types share a local path only if the application deliberately registers a custom path equal to another type's default suffix (258/339 vs 178); no ordinary configuration does that, so binding the token to the path rather than to the endpoint/event type looks harmless.

masking: Fixing T4 widens T1: once _build_path_map returns every registered path, the paths that were rejected as unknown at dispatcher.py:283-284 become routable and, with no _tokens entry at 286, dispatch unauthenticated.
Fixing T1 makes T3 observable: setup() would then create a webhook whose endpoint teardown(cleanup=True) cannot find, because it derives endpoints from DEFAULT_SUFFIXES at dispatcher.py:144-147.

Fixing T1 for any path beyond handlers[0] without T4 stores a token at dispatcher.py:112 for a path that the path map (182) cannot route, so TONAPI deliveries for it raise 'Unknown webhook path' at 283-284.

conflicts.what: The cheapest fix for T5 — reject any path whose _tokens lookup is None at dispatcher.py:286-287 — also rejects the tokenless dispatch that tests/webhook/test_dispatcher.py:60-83 and 131-141 require and that T1's fix must keep working for callers with no client (client is optional, dispatcher.py:45).

T1's natural fix enumerates paths through the paths property (dispatcher.py:163-170), but returning more than one path per event type to satisfy T4 breaks the documented dict[WebhookEventType, str] shape (docs/webhooks/guide.mdx:176) and its consumers (examples/webhook_fastapi.py:101-102, examples/webhook_aiohttp.py:100-101), so T4 needs a separate path iterator rather than a change to paths.

T1 creates per-path webhooks while teardown matches endpoints built from DEFAULT_SUFFIXES (dispatcher.py:143-145); the two must agree on one path-to-endpoint mapping or cleanup silently skips every custom path while its token stays live.

fairness_risks: Tokenless dispatch is must-keep-working: test_all_event_types_dispatch (tests/webhook/test_dispatcher.py:60-83) and test_custom_path (131-141) call process() with no Authorization and no client; a blanket 'token required' rule contradicts them.

_tokens is written directly by tests/webhook/test_dispatcher.py:190 as a local-path-keyed dict, and the field's comment says 'path -> secret token' (dispatcher.py:68); re-keying the store by endpoint URL or by (path, event_type) breaks that test and the documented key.

dispatcher.paths must stay dict[WebhookEventType, str] (docs/webhooks/guide.mdx:176, examples/webhook_fastapi.py:101-102, examples/webhook_aiohttp.py:100-101); a fix that returns several paths per event type breaks the documented route-wiring pattern.

Custom paths are stored verbatim (dispatcher.py:258, 339) while default paths carry the dispatcher URL prefix (dispatcher.py:63, 178); an app mounted under a prefix legitimately passes request.url.path with that prefix (examples/webhook_fastapi.py:85), so any check or normalisation for T1 must not refuse the prefixed form.

teardown(cleanup=True) is documented as best-effort and subscriptions persist across restarts (docs/webhooks/guide.mdx:166); a rule that requires deleting or unsubscribing every webhook contradicts that behaviour.

A path with a trailing slash or a doubled separator is a legitimate delivery shape; failing closed as 'Unknown webhook path' (dispatcher.py:283-284) is acceptable, but silently treating the same path as tokenless would refuse a legitimate input.

design.why: Four independent edit sites, each with its own judgement and a different dismissal argument: T1 at setup() (dispatcher.py:106-112, the report-described route and the warm-up), T4 at the two path-enumeration implementations (163-170 and 180-182, a how-type truncation a minimal setup-only fix reproduces), T3 at teardown (137-147, the twin a setup-only fix leaves broken and whose custom webhooks then never get unsubscribed), and T2 at registration (258-260, 341-343, a lifecycle hole gradeable with a fake client while the no-client tests stay green). It spans three mechanisms (M4, M2, M6) and two model profiles (T1 both, T2 deepseek, T3/T4 mimo). T5 is excluded because closing it contradicts the documented and tested no-client mode, and T6 is excluded because it needs a deliberately colliding path and would be a contrived behavioural test.
